properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10-19
feet, with local sets of 20-22 feet. Peak surf is expected from
late Wednesday through Thursday night. Dangerous rip currents
expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM to 10 AM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and
harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is
likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible, especially to
Pismo and Cayucos piers. There is an increased risk for ocean
drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea.
Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches
and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There is a chance for the coastal flood
advisory to be extended through later Thursday to cover the
secondary high tide in the evening.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 17 at 2:15PM PST until November 19 at 10:00AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.On the St Johns River at Astor, the river is forecast to continue to
rise through Moderate flood stage into next week due to strong
onshore flow causing a surge up the river as well as additional heavy
rainfall expected across the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with
several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals.
Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely
submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with
yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads
flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on
Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 3:30 AM EST Thursday the stage was 3.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 3:30 AM EST Thursday was 3.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.7 feet early Monday
morning. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

FFWMTR

The National Weather Service in San Francisco has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Timber burn area in...
Western Monterey County in central California...

* Until 830 PM PST.

* At 705 PM PST, CHP has reported an observed debris flow into NB
Highway One lanes in the vicinity of Big Sur Lodge and boulders in
the roadway at Hurricane Point. A car was reported stuck in the
debris flow near Big Sur. Doppler radar and automated rain gauges
indicated that heavy rain was falling over the Timber Burn Area.
Between 3 and 6 inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall
rate is 0.5 to 0.75 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts
of 1 to 3 inches are possible in the warned area. Conditions remain
favorable for additional moderate to heavy rainfall due to
orographic lift as the main rainband exits the county. Flash
flooding is ongoing. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will
result in debris flow moving through the Drainages within Lafler,
Castro and Graves Canyons, as well as drainages between Grimes and
Castro Canyons. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud,
vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding in and around the Timber Burn Area.

SOURCE...Law enforcement reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Timber Burn Area.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
portions of CA Highway 1 and the Los Padres National Forecast from
Andrew Molera State Park to Partington Ridge including the town of
Big Sur.

At 5:43 PM PST CHP reported a debris flow across NB Highway 1 lanes
in the vicinity of Big Sur Lodge. One hour rain rates have crossed
0.7" with additional heavy rain expected this evening into tomorrow
as scattered showers with the potential for moderate to heavy rain
and thunderstorms. CHP additionally reported boulders in the NB lane
of Highway One at Hurricane Point at 6:11 PM local time. CHP reported
a car stuck in the debris flow at Big Sur.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 16 at 1:25AM EST until November 18 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Brevard, FL; Orange, FL; Osceola, FL; Seminole, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northwestern Brevard County in east central Florida...
Southeastern Orange County in east central Florida...
Northeastern Osceola County in east central Florida...
Southeastern Seminole County in east central Florida...
Southern Volusia County in east central Florida...

* WHEN...Until 1000 AM EST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 756 AM EST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 2 inches are expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Orlando, Oviedo, Winter Springs, Winter Park, Wedgefield, Bithlo,
Avalon Park, Christmas, Chuluota, University Of Central Florida,
Azalea Park, Goldenrod, Orlando International Airport, Conway,
Lone Cabbage Fish Camp, Oak Ridge and Belle Isle.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

feet expected above this elevation; accumulations around 4 feet
above 8,000 feet. Winds could gust as high as 45 mph.

* WHERE...Sierra Nevada above 5,000 feet.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday.

hazardous conditions will impact daily travel. Gusty winds could

properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 17 at 4:31PM PST until November 20 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Hanford CA
properties.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Persons should consider delaying all travel. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution. Consider taking a winter storm
kit along with you, including such items as tire chains, booster
cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets and extra clothing. Also take
water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, an increased risk for
sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 12
to 17 ft. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.2 ft of
inundation above ground level is likely in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory,
large breaking waves of 18 to 24 ft with up to 30 ft at favored
breakpoints along the coast from this afternoon through Friday
morning.

* WHERE...San Francisco County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 10 AM PST Friday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 4 PM PST this
afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM this
afternoon to 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling
people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting
in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of
drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without
warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 7:15 AM
Thursday and 1.1 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 7:45 AM Friday.
These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will
enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide
varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast
and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 18 at 8:08AM PST until November 20 at 10:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swimmers should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf
conditions.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10-
19 feet, with local sets of 20-22 feet. Peak surf is expected
from late Wednesday through Thursday night. Dangerous rip
currents expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor
coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM to 10 AM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is
likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible, especially
to Pismo and Cayucos piers. There is an increased risk for
ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out
to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There is a chance for the coastal flood
advisory to be extended through later Thursday to cover the
secondary high tide in the evening.
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 17 at 8:32PM PST until November 20 at 9:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in

properties.description:
AVWREV

The following message is transmitted at the request of the U.S.
Forest Service Sierra Avalanche Center.

BACKCOUNTRY AVALANCHE WARNING

IMMEDIATE BROADCAST REQUESTED

05:30 PST Thu Nov 19 2026

The Sierra Avalanche Center in Truckee has issued a BACKCOUNTRY
AVALANCHE WARNING for the following areas: NWS Reno NV - NVZ002
(Greater Lake Tahoe)...CAZ072 (Greater Lake Tahoe (CA))

* WHAT...HIGH avalanche danger exists in the backcountry. Large
avalanches are expected across backcountry terrain.

* WHERE...Central Sierra Nevada Mountains between Yuba Pass (Hwy 49)
on the north and Ebbetts Pass (Hwy 4) on the south, including the
greater Lake Tahoe area. This applies only to backcountry areas,
not to ski areas and highways where avalanche mitigation programs
exist.

* WHEN...In effect from Thu 05:30 PST to Fri 04:00 PST.

* IMPACTS...Significant amounts of new snow and wind are creating
dangerous avalanche conditions in the backcountry. The new snow is
overloading a weak snowpack in some upper elevation areas.
Avalanches could run down into treed terrain.

* PRECAUTIONARY / PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...Very dangerous avalanche
conditions exist in the backcountry. Traveling in, near, or below
backcountry avalanche terrain is not recommended during HIGH
avalanche danger.

Consult https://www.sierraavalanchecenter.org/ or www.avalanche.org
for more detailed information.

Similar avalanche danger may exist at locations outside the coverage
area of this or any avalanche center.

properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

surf and coastal flooding issues are expected next week.

properties.description:
FFWMTR

The National Weather Service in San Francisco has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Plaskett burn area in...
South Central Monterey County in central California...

* Until 830 PM PST.

* At 706 PM PST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain falling over the Plaskett Burn Area. Between 2 and 5
inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 0.5 to
0.75 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches
are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar
will result in debris flow moving through the Alder, Plaskett, and
Prewitt Creeks. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud,
vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding in and around the Plaskett Burn Area.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

properties.instruction:

The following message is transmitted at the request of the U.S.
Forest Service Sierra Avalanche Center.

BACKCOUNTRY AVALANCHE WATCH

IMMEDIATE BROADCAST REQUESTED

08:55 PST Wed Nov 18 2026

The Sierra Avalanche Center in Truckee has issued a BACKCOUNTRY
AVALANCHE WATCH for the following areas:
NWS Reno NV - NVZ002 (Greater Lake Tahoe)...CAZ072 (Greater Lake Tahoe (CA))

* WHAT...HIGH avalanche danger is anticipated in the backcountry
from around sunset on Wednesday into early Friday morning.

* WHERE...Central Sierra Nevada Mountains between Yuba Pass (Hwy
49) on the north and Ebbetts Pass(Hwy 4) on the south,
including the greater Lake Tahoe area. This applies only to
backcountry areas, not to ski areas and highways where avalanche
mitigation programs exist.

* WHEN...In effect from Wed 08:55 PST to Thu 05:00 PST.

* IMPACTS...Significant snowfall may lead to widespread avalanche
activity in the mountains. Large avalanches capable of burying
or injuring people could occur in backcountry areas.

* PRECAUTIONARY / PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...Very dangerous
avalanche conditions could occur in the backcountry. Traveling
in, near, or below backcountry avalanche terrain during HIGH
avalanche danger is not recommended.

Consult https://www.sierraavalanchecenter.org/ or
www.avalanche.org for more detailed information.

Similar avalanche danger may exist at locations outside
the coverage area of this or any avalanche center.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 15 at 1:49PM EST until November 18 at 3:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.On the St Johns River at Astor, the river is forecast to continue to
rise through Moderate flood stage into next week due to strong
onshore flow causing a surge up the river as well as additional heavy
rainfall  expected across the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with
several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals.
Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely
submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with
yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads
flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on
Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 3.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Wednesday was 3.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.6 feet Sunday
evening. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with
yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads
flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on
Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EST Tuesday was 2.7 feet.

morning. Additional rises are possible thereafter.

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Ongoing extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River
has caused the river near Cocoa to rise through Major Flood Stage.
Additional heavy rainfall over the next 48 hours will continue to
produce river rises, bringing record flood levels at this point
overnight Thursday into Friday morning. this weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This is forecast to approach and surpass the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:15 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 17.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:15 PM EST Wednesday was 17.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 17.5 feet.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Ongoing extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River
has caused the river near Cocoa to rise through Major Flood Stage and
has now quickly passed record flood stage. Additional heavy rainfall
over the next 48 hours will continue to produce river rises above
record flood levels through late week and into this weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This passes the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 5:15 AM EST Thursday the stage was 18.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 5:15 AM EST Thursday was 18.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 18.2 feet
today.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 17 at 1:28AM EST until November 19 at 1:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, an increased risk for
sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 12
to 17 ft. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.3 ft of
inundation above ground level is likely in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory,
Large breaking waves of 15 to 18 ft along the coast from this
afternoon through Thursday afternoon.

* WHERE...San Francisco County.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through this afternoon.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 5 AM today to 10 AM PST
Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM today to 4 PM
PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling
people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting
in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of
drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without
warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 6:45 AM
today and 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 7:15 AM
Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific
Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 18 at 3:25AM PST until November 19 at 10:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone

conditions.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, an increased risk for
sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 12
to 17 ft. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.3 ft of
inundation above ground level is likely in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory,
Large breaking waves of 15 to 18 ft along the coast from
Wednesday afternoon through Thursday afternoon.

* WHERE...San Francisco County.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Wednesday
afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 5 AM Wednesday
to 10 AM PST Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM
Wednesday to 4 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling
people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting
in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of
drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without
warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 6:45 AM
Wednesday and 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 7:15 AM
Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific
Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 17 at 2:27PM PST until November 19 at 10:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swimmers should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf
conditions.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is
possible.

abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.

time):
* Port Chicago: 1.0 ft above normal (5.9 ft MLLW) at 9:10 AM
Wed 11/18, 1.3 ft above normal (6.2 ft MLLW) at 9:41 AM Thu
11/19, 1.6 ft above normal (6.5 ft MLLW) at 10:07 AM Fri
11/20, and 2.0 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 10:32 AM Sat
11/21.
* West Sacramento: 1.4 ft above normal (5.7 ft MLLW) at 12:09
PM Wed 11/18, 1.6 ft above normal (6.0 ft MLLW) at 12:37 PM
Thu 11/19, 1.9 ft above normal (6.3 ft MLLW) at 1:04 PM Fri
11/20, and 2.3 ft above normal (6.6 ft MLLW) at 1:35 PM Sat
11/21.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +6.5 ft at 11:00 AM Wed 11/18,
+6.9 ft at 12:00 PM Thu 11/19, +6.4 ft at 12:00 PM Fri 11/20,
and +6.8 ft at 1:00 PM Sat 11/21.

- These predictions include up to +2.1 feet of storm surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
Timing of high tide may vary by several hours throughout the
San Francisco Bay and Delta.

* Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre
dictions.html?id=9415144
* West Sacramento: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatide
predictions.html?id=9416131

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 19 at 1:19AM EST until November 21 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

seawalls and docks will be overtopped. Boaters can expect less
clearance under fixed bridges. Motorists should remember that
persistent puddles around the times of high tide are almost
certain to contain a mix of saltwater.
